findings.title: Whole-session spend is misrepresented as cost displaced by one recurring sequence
findings.what: For every matching session, the detector adds the session's entire estimated cost, then tells the judge and user that this amount is manual work the particular n-gram would displace. Sessions can contain substantial unrelated work and multiple candidate sequences, so the same spend can be fully attributed to several recommendations. The arithmetic sum is reproducible, but the attribution claim is not evidence-backed.
findings.fix: Replace displacedCost with a clearly labeled whole-session context metric, or calculate an attributable sequence cost using documented per-call/token evidence and retain those artifact references in the finding.
findings.acceptance: Add a session containing the recurring three-tool sequence plus unrelated expensive activity and verify the finding does not claim the full session cost is displaced; emitted evidence must identify the fields used for any attributed dollar amount.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed line 117 sums costBySession for each entire matching session, lines 162-177 label that total displaced, and the test at lines 47-53 explicitly expects 1.5 + 2.5 with no sequence-level allocation.

findings.title: Boomerang rate claims post-shipment rework without shipment or file-level evidence
findings.what: Candidates contain an in-session checkpoint score and only the total number of high-churn files. They contain no shipped timestamp, revert/retouch event, affected file, temporal ordering, or link between the session and those files. Nevertheless, the judge is asked to classify bounce-back and the result states code was re-touched shortly after it shipped. A judge rationale cannot create missing provenance, so the recommendation is not reproducible from its evidenceRefs.
findings.fix: Either rename and constrain the output to an interpreted retry-storm rate, or join candidates to concrete shipment and subsequent revert/retouch events with timestamps and file/session provenance before calculating a boomerang rate.
findings.acceptance: A fixture with high checkpoint churn but no shipment or later retouch must emit no shipped-boomerang claim; a positive fixture must cite the shipped event, later mutation, affected artifact, and timestamps used to reproduce the numerator and denominator.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass confirmed candidate construction only copies score/churn/burstRate plus churnFiles.length, the prompt receives only those fields, while lines 213-218 assert post-shipment retouch. The test derives 67% solely from a fake judge keyed on session IDs and asserts only session evidence.
